look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: tumble windmillgrass often carries LONG one-sided radiating racemes in SEVERAL well-separated whorls or tiers along the upper flowering axis, sometimes ending in an upright terminal branch. Unlike hooded windmillgrass, its mature upper sterile lemma is not an inflated round hood, and the awns are longer. Check two measured awns and whorl placement before committing to a species name.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted POWO species and Texas state-level native distribution; source-pool admission approved; three target-zone county confirmations not independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial windmillgrass with ~10–16 racemes in separated whorls; ripe panicle may detach and tumble.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Fertile lemma awn ~4.8–9 mm; sterile lemma awn ~3.2–7 mm. Upper sterile floret is not a conspicuously swollen round hood.
best_field_traits: Awn measurements on fertile and sterile lemmas
Upright terminal branch and sometimes intact detachable head
crew_field_walkthrough: Use the whole held seedhead and/or the botanical illustration to locate the main vertical flowering axis.
Check whether long branches arise from more than one level along the axis; in photographs, overlapping branches can hide this, so document it with a clean side-on full head.
Dissect mature spikelets and measure the fertile-lemma and sterile-lemma awns SEPARATELY; head shape alone overlaps the hybrid.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole intact head SIDE VIEW with separated levels of long branches and ruler.
Individual branching junctions annotated at multiple levels of one intact culm.
Two mature one-sided spikelets in hand lens: fertile awn (~4.8–9 mm) versus upper sterile awn (~3.2–7 mm) separately.
Real rooted crown and matched C. cucullata/hybrid photographs.
morphology_keys.field_photo_limitations: Separate photo lesson can include the original USDA botanical illustration, but it must be labeled as an ILLUSTRATION, not counted as a photo or as a measured modern specimen.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with hooded windmillgrass, C. verticillata favors well-separated whorls of longer racemes and much longer fertile/sterile lemma awns; unlike C. virgata, it is normally perennial with multi-tier flowering branches, not an annual terminal fan. The hybrid C. × subdolichostachya may resemble it substantially, so use mature sterile-lemma anatomy.
comparisons.cautions: Head color, overall windmill appearance and awn length alone can mislead. Inspect a fully mature spikelet with scale; hybrid intermediates must remain uncertain.

diagnostic_image_needs: Whole mature head and basal crown with scale
Dissected mature fertile and sterile lemmas with millimeter scale
Matched local Chloris comparison showing diagnostic whorl and awn differences

visual_comparison.title: Chloris verticillata — windmillgrass field ID
visual_comparison.subtitle: Actual installed photographs checked for visible structures; an image of a different species is explicitly labeled look-alike. Do not mislabel a whole raceme as a microscopic lemma.

items.label: 1 · Long branching head across fingers
items.image_role: Handheld actual long one-sided spikelet-bearing racemes and flowering axis
items.caption: Long greenish racemes arise along the upper axis and individual spikelets occupy one side. The full extent of tiers is partly cut off, so do not claim exact whorl count or awn lengths.
items.why_it_matters: The most useful existing REAL flowering photo, better than drawing alone.
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.photo_status: Existing exact-source physical image visually examined on 2026-10-20; arrows point only at structures that are visible. Source photograph taxon ID not independently voucher-verified; license/credit retained, public gate separately required.

items.label: 2 · Rooted perennial-looking plant
items.image_role: A vegetative grass bunch with narrow blades and stems near ground
items.caption: The photo shows narrow leaves and a rooted-looking patch, with a hand near a reproductive stem. Roots and age were not checked; the perennial habit is not independently established by this image.
items.why_it_matters: Shows leaf and crown context without inventing roots or annual/perennial state.

items.label: LOOK-ALIKE — Chloris cucullata (different species)
items.caption: The compared photograph belongs to Chloris cucullata, not Chloris verticillata. Notice overlapping windmill forms, then confirm identity with the unpictured sterile lemma and awn anatomy.
items.why_it_matters: Shows why broad seedhead shape alone often cannot prove the exact species.
